quantum-fundamentals.alt: A classical bit showing only 0 or 1 beside a qubit on a Bloch sphere holding both at once
quantum-fundamentals.caption: A bit is one of two values. A qubit is a combination of both until measured.

quantum-fundamentals.alt: A spinning coin shown mid-spin as both heads and tails, then collapsed to one face after landing
quantum-fundamentals.caption: The spinning coin: genuinely both, not secretly one. Landing is the measurement.

quantum-fundamentals.alt: Two waves approaching, adding constructively, then cancelling destructively
quantum-fundamentals.caption: Amplitudes add and cancel. Interference is what separates quantum from merely random.

quantum-fundamentals.alt: A probability amplitude being squared to give a measurement probability, with bar charts
quantum-fundamentals.caption: Born's rule: probability is the square of the amplitude — which is why amplitudes may be negative.

quantum-fundamentals.alt: Two quantum amplitudes cancelling exactly to zero and the resulting flat distribution
quantum-fundamentals.caption: Perfect cancellation. No classical probability can do this.

quantum-gates.alt: Pauli Y and Z gates shown as 180 degree rotations about the Y and Z axes
quantum-gates.caption: Y and Z rotate about their own axes; Z changes phase without changing probabilities.

quantum-gates.alt: The Hadamard gate mapping ket zero to the plus state on the Bloch sphere
quantum-gates.caption: Hadamard moves |0⟩ to the equator, creating an even superposition.

quantum-gates.alt: A Bloch sphere with X, Y and Z axes labelled and the six cardinal states marked
quantum-gates.caption: The six cardinal states. Every pure single-qubit state lives on this surface.

quantum-entanglement.alt: A CNOT circuit with control and target, producing a Bell state from a superposed control
quantum-entanglement.caption: CNOT applied to a superposed control does not pick a branch — it correlates both.

quantum-entanglement.alt: The four Bell states in Dirac notation with the circuit preparing each
quantum-entanglement.caption: All four Bell states are one Hadamard and one CNOT, differing only in the input.

quantum-entanglement.alt: GHZ and W states compared, showing GHZ entanglement destroyed by qubit loss while W survives
quantum-entanglement.caption: Lose one qubit: GHZ shatters, W keeps its entanglement. That tradeoff decides the protocol.

quantum-cryptography-qkd.alt: A CHSH chart showing the classical limit of 2 and the quantum value 2√2 ≈ 2.83
quantum-cryptography-qkd.caption: Quantum correlations exceed any local hidden-variable theory. Nobel Prize, 2022.
